subject: Urgent: Quantify.ai production latency & reserved throughput depletion
messages:
From: Tom Gardner <tgardner@quantify.ai>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@quantify.ai>
Date: 2028-07-23T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Production errors and rising latency - urgent

Dylan —

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 500s and tail latency this morning across our inference endpoints (predict.quantify.ai). Our engineers are throttling traffic but it's impacting customer SLAs. Your dashboard shows our dedicated GPU pool is hitting sustained headroom exhaustion and the reserved throughput counter is dropping well below our committed level.

Can you confirm what's happening, and how soon we can get relief? This is causing live customers to see timeouts. I can jump on a call if helpful.

Attaching a quick export of our error spike and timeline.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Gardner
Head of Platform — Quantify.ai

Attachment: quantify_prod_errors_20280723.csv (csv, 32KB)

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
To: Tom Gardner <tgardner@quantify.ai>, Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@quantify.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-23T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and rising latency - urgent

Tom — thanks for the data and flagging.

Quick summary from our side after the first pass:
- Observed a rapid increase in concurrent token-in-flight for QNT-4523 around 07:45 PDT; dedicated pool consumed headroom and autoscale did not add nodes quickly enough for the workload profile.
- A subset of requests hit a throttling path that caused retries and amplified queueing, resulting in 5xx spikes and 95/99th latency growth.

Immediate next steps (we've kicked these off):
1) Engineering: enabling emergency burst capacity for your pool (30 mins to provision) — Marissa is coordinating.
2) Ops: enabling a temporary model fallback for non-critical routes to a smaller quantized variant to reduce per-token latency — Vivek running validation.
3) Rate-limit guidance: Ask Quantify to move non-essential batch jobs to a 60-minute window to reduce sustained sustained concurrency.

I'll keep you updated every 30 mins until stable and propose an exec touchpoint if we need capacity reallocation beyond burst.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-23T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Actioning burst & fallback — immediate ops checklist

Internal —

Summary: Dylan already briefed the customer. Tech details below and asks for exec alignment if escalation grows.

Observed telemetry:
- Pool qnt-prod-3: GPU utilization 98% across the cluster; queuing depth up 12x vs baseline; average token service time normal but tail multiplies due to KV cache churn.
- Autoscaler decision loops delayed due to sudden sequence-length shift from recent model update (longer prompts).

Immediate ops items (owner):
- Marissa: request burst pool (N+2 liveness) from infra and pre-warm with QNT traffic (ETA 30m).
- Vivek: validate quantized fallback's output parity on a representative prompt set (ETA 20m) and prepare config rollback plan.
- Priyom: prepare a customer-facing mitigation timeline and coordinate messaging with CS and legal if credits are requested.

Exec ask: If burst proves insufficient, we will need authorization to reassign reserved capacity from a low-priority account for 24 hours. This requires approval from Revenue Ops and the CTO desk.

Attachments: qnt_playbook_shortlist.pdf

Marissa Cole
Sr. Technical Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-23T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Actioning burst & fallback — model validation

Ran quick parity checks on the 50-sample prompt set from Quantify: quantized-1b model returns equivalent intent and top-3 tokens match in 92% of cases; latency median down ~35%, p99 down ~48%. No catastrophic regressions observed.

Risks: outputs for long multi-turn prompts have slightly different tokenization boundaries — recommend limiting fallback to /predict-batched and chat-lite routes for first 2 hrs.

I'll mark the fallback as ready. If exec authorizes cross-account headroom reassign, we'll need an ops window (10m) to shift reservations.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-23T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Actioning burst & fallback — exec approval request

Leadership —

We are in a fast-moving customer-impact incident for Quantify.ai (QNT-4523). Burst capacity is being provisioned but only covers ~40% of the 15-minute spike. Fallback plan validated by infra reduces tail latency materially.

Decision needed: Temporary reassign 200 reserved units from non-critical account PULSE-LOWPRIO to Quantify for a 24-hour window starting ASAP. Impact: possible SLA/credit for the donor account; recommended mitigation: automated notification and 10% credit holdback to compensate.

Recommended next steps for execs:
- Approve temporary reservation shift (yes/no)
- If approved, designate an owner from Revenue Ops to sign off on credits and customer comms
- Stand up a 15-min exec bridge in 30 mins to review stabilization and decide permanent remediation (capacity increase or revision to autoscaler heuristics).

Please reply with approval or questions.

—Priyom Das
Head of Solutions & Response, Redwood Inference

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
To: Tom Gardner <tgardner@quantify.ai>, Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@quantify.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-23T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and rising latency - urgent

Tom / Sofia —

Update: we provisioned emergency burst capacity (N+2 nodes) and enabled a limited model fallback on non-critical endpoints at 15:22 PDT. Early telemetry shows error rate falling (5xx down 85% from peak) and p99 latency improving ~40%.

Pending items:
- We requested a temporary reassign of 200 reserved units; awaiting exec approval (internal). If approved we'll keep it for 24 hours to give space for a stable autoscaler and to roll a safer model update.
- We recommend holding non-essential batch jobs off-peak for the next 6 hours.

Next touch: I'll send a stabilization report at +4 hours and propose a follow-up call with our infra leads to determine a long-term capacity uplift or autoscaler heuristic change. Sorry again for the disruption — appreciate your patience.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
